pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 20 Introduction July 15, 2026 CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement INTRODUCTION Support: 01 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and Paralympics (LA28), which includes the Summer Olympics (July 14-30, 2028) and Summer Paralympics (August 15-27, 2028), will establish a Games Route Network (GRN) with dedicated lanes for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues and ensure athletes and Game personnel get to their events and venues on time. The GRN will establish a temporary network of roads, freeways, expressways, highways, arterials, local roads, and managed lanes to provide a safe, fast, and reliable transportation system. 02 During the Games, in order to facilitate the movement of athletes and Games personnel, some of the existing traffic control devices on roadways included in the established GRN will need to be changed temporarily, to allow identification of the priority lanes that have been dedicated in GRN for athletes and Game personnel travel. This will be accomplished by using “LA28” white legend or black legend on light blue background as a sign plaque or sign panel and using it as a word message pavement marking. National MUTCD has not assigned the meaning of light blue color, currently, it has reserved it for future designation. Any use of light blue color on a traffic control device will not be in compliance with the MUTCD, requiring permission to experiment. At some locations, in addition to the LA28 sign plaque or panel, the “PERMIT ONLY” black legend on white background will also be used as a sign plaque or sign panel and in white legend as a pavement marking. 03 To save costs, expedite implementation and for fiscal responsibility, since the change is needed temporarily, instead of removing existing signs and installing new or special traffic signs, most of the changes will be limited to changing existing traffic signs. New signs will be used only when existing signs are not available at the location or impractical to change. The “LA28” sign plaque will be added to some of the existing traffic signs, a portion of some traffic signs will be overlayed with the “LA28” panel, while some of the traffic signs would be covered during the games. The PERMIT ONLY plaque and panel will be used in conjunction with the LA28 plaque or panel, on some of the traffic signs. The “LA28” pavement markings, in conjunction with, or without, the PERMIT ONLY pavement markings will be installed in some lanes of the GRN roadways. LA28 traffic control devices will be installed from Fall 2027 through July 1, 2028. The LA28 signs will be covered when installed and uncovered starting June 1, 2028. The facilities will be restored beginning September 1, 2028. 04 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and Paralympics (LA28) being an atypical large-scale special event, it necessitates the use of unique identifier, to draw attention to the LA28 traffic signs. Using “LA28” white or black legend on light blue background serves this purpose by aiding recognition and quicker comprehension of the dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games, while keeping the message simple. Using the light blue color for the background was chosen as this color is already included in the National Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) and has been identified as being appropriate for use in conveying traffic control information. The light blue color in the MUTCD is reserved for future designation and not assigned any specific purpose. The proposed use of the light blue color during the Games does not comply with the National MUTCD, it requires approval to experiment from FHWA. 05 Caltrans prepared a request for permission to experiment for the use of light blue color as the background color on LA28 sign plaques and sign panels. The experiment was approved by Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) on August 13, 2025. CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 21 Introduction July 15, 2026 08 In general, the CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement contents correlate to the CA MUTCD (and National MUTCD) Parts, Chapters and Sections in the same sequence, heading and numbering and retaining the same titles. In instances where there is no corresponding Section, Figure or Table in the CA MUTCD or National MUTCD for a topic in the CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement, the topic is given a new number and include “LA28” in parentheses to indicate that it is specific only for LA28. 09 The CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement includes only the additional section, figure and table contents that are needed for use on GRN roadways during the Los Angles 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics competition as part of the experimentation request. Current CA MUTCD, including its section, figure and table contents, will be used for all traffic control devices used on GRN roadways during Los Angles 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics. CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement provides only additional content that are specific to dedicated lanes on GRN roadways and for use only during the Los Angles 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics to support the experimentation request.

pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 22 Chapter 1C - Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations Used in this Manual July 15, 2026 Part 1 General PART 1 GENERAL CHAPTER 1C. DEFINITIONS, ACRONYMS, AND ABBREVIATIONS USED IN THIS MANUAL Section 1C.02 Definitions of Words and Phrases Used in this Manual The following is added to this section: Standard: 03 The following words and phrases, when used in this Manual, shall have the following meanings: 92a. Games Route Network (GRN) - Network of existing roads connecting Los Angles 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics competition and key non-competition venues involving a wide range of traffic management measures. As per California Vehicle Code Section 21655.10, vehicles with a permit only will be allowed to use the dedicated lanes on roadways in GRN. 97a. GRN Lane(s) - Specific preferential lanes that are used as dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues and are included in the established GRN. Section 1C.03 Meanings of Acronyms and Abbreviations Used in this Manual The following is added to this section: Support: 02 The following list of acronyms are related to traffic control devices and provided for ease of use and as a handy reference: 25a. GRN Games Route Network 104a. LA28 Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and Paralympics 03 The acronym “LA28” refers to the name of the event, named by the host city plus the 2-digit year (e.g. Paris24). Abbreviating the year allows the word message to be as brief as practical while keeping it simple, allowing for easier accommodation when used on the plaque, panel or as word message pavement marking.

pages.title: PART 2
pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 25 Chapter 2A - General July 15, 2026 Part 2 Signs PART 2 SIGNS CHAPTER 2A. GENERAL Section 2A.01 Function and Purpose of Signs The following is added to this section: Standard: 05 The provisions of Part 2 regarding signs in general (Chapter 2A), regulatory signs (Chapters 2B and 2G), guide signs (Chapters 2D, 2E and 2G) and changeable message signs (Chapter 2L) shall apply to all roadways included in the established GRN in locations specified by Caltrans experimentation request to FHWA. Section 2A.02 Standardization of Application The following is added to this section: Guidance: 07 The LA28 sign plaque and LA28 sign panel should be used only where deemed necessary or desirable and justified by engineering judgment, as provided in Sections 1D.03 and 1C.02 (Paragraph 3, Definition 76). Option: 08 The LA28 sign plaque or the LA28 sign panel (see Figure 2A-101(LA28)) may be used on any existing or new regulatory or guide sign included in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement, where engineering judgment determines the need to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. 09 If used, the LA28 sign plaque or the LA28 sign panel may be combined with the word message PERMIT ONLY in black legend on a white background at some locations, where engineering judgment determines it is needed. Standard: 10 If the Transportation Demand Management (TDM) strategies implemented in the established GRN, require regulatory or operational measures different than those existing, the existing permanent regulatory and guide signs that are no longer applicable, and potentially could be confusing or misleading, they shall be covered or removed and superseded by the appropriate temporary regulatory or guide signs during the games. 11 The LA28 sign plaque and the LA28 sign panel shall be rectangular and shall consist of the word message “LA28” (refer to Section 2A.06 for legend and background colors). The LA28 legend shall be a single line for horizontal configuration. The LA28 legend for the vertical configuration shall be 2 lines, with LA legend in line 1 and 28 legend in line 2. 12 If used, the LA28 sign plaque shall be added as a header plaque above any existing or new regulatory, warning, or guide sign included in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement, to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. If using the LA28 sign header plaque in the vertical configuration, it shall be placed on the left edge of the sign. 13 If used, the LA28 sign panel shall be used as a header panel and affixed to the face of a sign to overlay a portion of any existing or new regulatory, warning, or guide sign included in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement, to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. If using the LA28 sign header panel in the horizontal configuration, it shall be placed in the top portion of the sign. If using the LA28 sign header panel in the vertical configuration, it shall be placed on the left edge of the sign. Option: 14 The LA28 sign panel may be used within an existing or new sign where engineering judgment determines the panel is needed. 15 The LA28 sign plaque and LA28 sign panel, each shall not be used alone. Support: 16 If signs using the LA28 sign plaque or LA28 sign panel need to be installed at new locations to identify GRN dedicated lanes during LA28 games, refer to Section 2A.13 in current CA MUTCD 2026.

pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 26 Chapter 2A - General July 15, 2026 Part 2 Signs Section 2A.04 Design of Signs The following is added to this section: Support: 02a In the provisions for the individual regulatory or guide signs included in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement, the general appearance of the legend, color, and size are shown in the CA MUTCD 2026 tables and illustrations and the sign specifications and are not always detailed in the text. 03a Detailed drawings of these standard regulatory and guide signs, alphabets, symbols, and arrows (see CA MUTCD 2026 Figure 2D-3) are shown in the “Standard Highway Signs and Markings” book. CA MUTCD 2026 Section 1A.05 contains information regarding how to obtain this publication. Standard: 06a The term legend shall include LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word messages for use on the sign plaque and as part of the sign panel to convey specific meaning. 07a Uniformity in design of the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY sign plaque and sign panel shall include shape, color, dimensions, legends, borders, and illumination or retroreflectivity. 08a Standardization of these sign plaque and sign panel does not preclude further improvement by minor changes in the proportion, width of borders, or layout of word messages, but all shapes and colors shall be as indicated. Support: 09a The daytime color specification limits and luminance factors (percent) for retroreflective material of the light blue color can be determined from Tables 1 and 1a of Appendix to 23 CFR Part 655, Subpart F. Caltrans and 3M conducted testing to establish a range of light blue color that will be used in this experiment. The trial test was initiated by developing samples of light blue color using FHWA daytime chromaticity coordinates. These samples were tested to measure their nighttime chromaticity coordinates. Refer to Table 2A-101(LA28) for daytime and nighttime chromaticity coordinates for light blue color. These coordinates will be verified using field and lab testing to ensure the light blue color is visible at night with comparable characteristics as during the daytime. Luminance is not defined for Type XI sheeting; cap Y values between 10 and 19 was recommended by 3M. 09b Caltrans plans to engage Caltrans Headquarters Division of Research and Information Systems and Headquarters Transportation Laboratory to conduct an off-roadway, closed-course, or laboratory evaluation and study. This evaluation study will test the use of black and white LA28 legend on the Caltrans identified light blue background color. The study will evaluate which color combination provides better contrast, when used for LA28 Sign Plaque and Sign Panel. This evaluation and testing will be the second initial step within this experimentation request, in advance of the actual deployment under this experimentation request of the sign plaques and sign panels during the games. 09c Any field testing, if needed, will be conducted within Caltrans Maintenance Yard or Caltrans facility, to determine the appropriate legend and background color combination, that provides better contrast for the LA28 word message, when used on sign plaques and sign panels. The decision to use legend color, black or white, for LA28 word message on the light blue colored background will be made in advance of the games and not during the games to avoid road user confusion and related safety concerns during the games. Only one color, either black or white, will be used as the legend color in the actual experiment during the games. Section 2A.05 Shapes The following is added to this section: Standard: 10 The standard shapes and standard proportions of existing regulatory and guide sign that are temporarily changed during LA28, shall be retained as much as practical, and comply with Table 2A-1. Color schemes using light blue color on specific signs are shown in the illustrations located in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement. Section 2A.07 Dimensions The following is added to this section: Guidance: 11 When LA28 sign plaque or LA28 sign panel are installed with larger sized signs, a corresponding increase in the size of the plaque or the panel and its legend should also be made. The resulting plaque or panel size should be approximately in the same relative proportion to the larger-sized sign as the conventional sized plaque or panel is to the conventional-sized sign. Standard: 12 The LA28 and PERMIT ONLY legends used on sign plaques and sign panels shall have letters and numerals that comply with the minimum height requirements shown in the Tables included in CA MUTCD 2026 for the roadway classifications and the specific signs that they supplement. Section 2A.08 Word Messages The following is added to this section: Standard: 20 Except as provided in Paragraph 21, the LA28 sign plaque and LA28 sign panel shall include only the legend “LA28” as a word message. Option: 21 The LA28 sign plaque or the LA28 sign panel may be combined with the word message PERMIT ONLY where engineering judgment determines it is needed. Standard: 22 The LA28 and PERMIT ONLY lettering used on sign plaque and sign panel shall be in upper-case letters and shall be of the Standard Alphabets as provided in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05). The unique letter forms used shall not be stretched, compressed, warped, or otherwise manipulated. Support: 23 Section 2D.03 contains information regarding the acceptable methods of modifying the length of a word for a given letter height and series for guide signs. Section 2A.09 Symbols The following is added to this section: Standard: 01a The LA28 Sign Plaque and Sign Panel shall not include any Olympic games, Para-Olympics symbol or any other symbol. The Olympic rings symbol shall not be used on, as part of, or in conjunction with the LA28 Sign Plaque or Sign Panel as its use is prohibited under the copyright laws. Support: 12 The Olympic rings represent only one of the two games that Los Angeles will be hosting during the time period covered under Caltrans experimentation request. Los Angeles will also be hosting the Paralympic Games. The International Paralympic Committee (IPC) is a completely separate organization with a different name, logo, and organizing body. Section 2A.11 Enhanced Conspicuity for Standard Signs The following is added to this section: Support: 07 This CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement is issued in support of Caltrans request for experimentation to FHWA is specifically for the use of light blue color as the background color for the “LA28” word message. The purpose of using light blue color as a background color for LA28 word message, is as a unique identifier to draw attention to the traffic sign plaques and traffic sign panels, and to aid recognition and quicker comprehension of the dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. Section 2A.13 Standardization of Location The following is added to this section: Guidance: 12a If engineering judgment determines the need to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games, at either existing sign locations or new locations with no signs, and space is limited for sign installation and there is a

pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 28 Chapter 2A - General July 15, 2026 Part 2 Signs demand for several different types of signs, an order of priority for sign installation should be established so as not to overload road users with too much information. 13a Because regulatory information is more critical to the road user than guidance information, any regulatory signs using LA28 sign plaque or LA28 sign panel whose location is critical should be displayed rather than guide signs that are using LA28 sign plaque or LA28 sign panel, in cases where conflicts occur. Information of a less critical nature should be moved to less critical locations or omitted. Section 2A.14 Overhead Sign Installations The following is added to this section: Option: 01a The LA28 sign plaque or the LA28 sign panel, including if it is combined with the word message PERMIT ONLY, may be used on any existing or new regulatory or guide Overhead signs on freeways and expressways, where engineering judgment determines the need to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. Section 2A.20 Excessive Use of Signs The following is added to this section: Guidance: 03c Installing new signs, including new signs at new locations to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games, should be avoided for fiscal responsibility and to avoid excessive signing and removal of these signs after the games. To save costs and expedite implementation, since the change is needed temporarily, opportunities to use the LA28 sign plaque or LA28 sign panel with the existing traffic signs should be considered, if signing is needed. Section 2A.21 Retroreflection and Illumination The following is added to this section: Standard: 03a The LA28 Sign Plaque and Sign Panel shall be retroreflective (see Section 2A.22) or illuminated to show the same shape and similar color by both day and night. Option: 07a Retroreflection of LA28 Sign Plaque and Sign Panel elements may be accomplished by the means shown in Table 2A-2(LA28). Standard: 09 The uniformity of the sign design shall be maintained without any decrease in visibility, legibility, or driver comprehension during either daytime or nighttime conditions.

PREFERENTIAL AND MANAGED LANE SIGNS Section 2G.01 Scope The following is added to this section: Support: 11 Specific preferential lanes will be used to designate Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues on roadways that are included in the established GRN during LA28 in locations specified by the supplement. Specific preferential lanes that are used as dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues and included in the established GRN, are referred to as “GRN lane(s)” in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement. Standard: 12 The provisions of Chapter 2G for regulatory and guide signs shall apply to all roadways included in the established GRN in locations specified by Caltrans experimentation request to FHWA. Section 2G.03 Regulatory Signs for Preferential Lanes - General The following is added to this section: Standard: 25 The provisions of Sections 2G.03 through 2G.07 regarding regulatory signs for preferential lanes shall apply to GRN dedicated lanes operated at all times or at certain times based on the needs of established GRN to allow Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues and ensure athletes and accredited persons make their events and venues on time. Such GRN lanes shall use changeable message signs or changeable message elements within static signs, or static signs to display the appropriate regulatory sign messages only when they are in effect. Option: 26 Regulatory signs or regulatory panels within the appropriate guide signs may be used to display the open/closed status of the GRN lane. 27 The LA28 sign plaque or the LA28 sign panel may be used on any regulatory sign included in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement, where engineering judgment determines the need to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. 28 If used, the LA28 sign plaque or the LA28 sign panel may be combined with the word message PERMIT ONLY in black legend on a white background where engineering judgment determines it is needed. Standard: 29 Regulatory signs applicable only to a dedicated GRN lane shall be distinguished from regulatory signs applicable to general- purpose lanes by the inclusion of the legend “LA28”, or “LA28” and “PERMIT ONLY” (see Figure 2G-1(LA28)). Refer to Section 2A.06 for "LA28" word legend and legend background colors. If used, the legend “PERMIT ONLY” color shall be black and the background color shall be white. Support: 30 The word message and light blue color background displayed on a particular GRN Lane regulatory sign will vary based on the specific type of allowed traffic and on other related operational constraints that have been established for a particular lane. Option: 31 Changeable message signs may supplement or substitute for static GRN Lane regulatory signs where travel conditions change or where multiple types of operational strategies (such as time of day requirements or vehicle types) are used and varied throughout the day or week, or on a real-time basis, to manage the use of, control of, or access to GRN lanes. Standard: 32 When changeable message signs (see Chapter 2L) are used as regulatory signs for GRN lanes, they shall be the required sign size and shall display the required letter height and legend format that corresponds to the type of roadway facility and design speed. Guidance: 33 When regulatory signs are used at new locations on conventional roads to facilitate GRN travel during LA28 games, the decision regarding whether to use a barrier-mounted, post-mounted, or overhead version of a particular type of sign should be based on an engineering judgment that considers the available space, the existing signs for the adjacent general-purpose traffic lanes, roadway and traffic characteristics, the proximity to existing overhead signs, the ability to install overhead signs, and any other unique local factors

CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 42 Chapter 2G - Preferential and Managed Lane Signs July 15, 2026 Part 2 Signs as overhead signs applicable only to the general-purpose lanes, the signs for the GRN lane should be separated laterally from the signs for the general-purpose lanes to the maximum extent practicable to minimize conflicting information, while maintaining their visual relationship to the lanes below necessitated by specific legend or arrows indicating lane assignment. Guidance: 35 On conventional roadways, existing signage and new sign installation locations (if needed) spacing should be determined by engineering judgment based on speed, block length, distances from adjacent intersections, and other site-specific considerations. Support: 36 The agencies that own and operate roadways included in the established GRN have the authority and responsibility to determine how they are operated and the GRN permit requirements. 37 Figures 2G-2(LA28) and 2G-3(LA28) illustrates the examples of LA28 sign panels on regulatory signs for the beginning, along the length, and at the end of contiguous GRN lanes that provide continuous access with the adjacent general purpose lanes. CHANGEABLE MESSAGE SIGNS Section 2L.01 Description of Changeable Message Signs The following is added to this section: Standard: 09 If used, provisions of Chapter 2G and Chapter 2L of CA MUTCD 2026 and this Supplement LA28 shall apply to changeable message signs used in GRN dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues that is included in the established GRN. Such GRN lanes shall use changeable message signs or changeable message elements within static signs to display the appropriate regulatory sign messages only when they are in effect. Support: 10 Refer to Sections 1D.08, 2G.01, and 2G.06, Figures 2G-8(LA28), 2G-9(LA28), and Tables 1D-101(LA28), 2A-2, and 2A-2(LA28) of CA MUTCD 2026 and its LA28 Supplement for more details on changeable message sign applications in GRN dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues that is included in the established GRN. Section 2L.02 Applications of Changeable Message Signs The following is added to this section: Option: 02a Any existing or new changeable message signs or portable changeable message signs may be used to display GRN messages, where engineering judgment determines the need to use GRN messages on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. Support: 02b Proposed GRN messages used on the changeable message signs and portable changeable message signs, such as LA28 PERMIT ONLY, LA28 PERMIT ONLY AHEAD, and LA28 PERMIT ONLY LEFT LANE are transportation-related messages. Standard: 02c GRN messages used on changeable message signs shall be used only if the changeable message signs or the portable changeable message signs are located in or on approaches to GRN dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues that is included in the established GRN. Messages must conform to message requirements, including those for abbreviations, included in Parts 1 and 2. Section 2L.05 Message Length and Units of Information The following is added to this section: Guidance: 12 When a CMS is used to display a GRN message, the message should be simple, direct, brief, legible, and clear (see Section 1D.01). GRN messages should be relevant to the road user on the roadway that is included in the established GRN, on which the message is displayed. 13 The GRN message should be appropriately shortened or otherwise modified to comply with the provisions of Section 2L.05 when it is displayed on a CMS. 14 The GRN message should be similar to the static GRN regulatory and guide sign legends that are included in CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement in Chapter 2G. Support: 15 Table 2L-101(LA28) provides examples of GRN messages for CMS that can be used in GRN dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues that is included in the established GRN.

GENERAL Section 3A.01 Standardization of Application The following is added to this section: Standard: 09 The provisions of Part 3 regarding markings in general, material, retroreflectivity (Chapter 3A), word pavement markings (Chapter 3B), preferential lane markings (Chapter 3E) and colored pavements (Chapter 3H) shall apply to all roadways included in the established GRN in locations specified by Caltrans experimentation request to FHWA. 10 When a Games Route Network (GRN) has been established with dedicated lanes for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues, the LA28 sign plaque, LA28 sign panel, including when combined with PERMIT ONLY message (see Chapters 2A, 2B, 2D, 2E and 2G) and LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings (see Chapters 3A, 3B, 3E and 3H) for these lanes shall be used to advise road users of GRN permit requirements and restrictions. Guidance: 11 The LA28 word pavement marking (see Figures 3B-107(LA28) and 3B-108(LA28)) should be used only where deemed necessary or desirable and justified by engineering judgment, as provided in Section 1D.03. 12 The LA28 word pavement markings in white color legend, without any background should only be used where the white legend color contrasts significantly with the adjoining paved areas. The LA28 word pavement marking can be used in combination with the black color to enhance contrast with adjoining paved areas. Option: 13 The LA28 word pavement marking may be used on any roadway that is included in the established GRN, where engineering judgment determines the need to identify GR dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. 14 To enhance the identification of GRN dedicated lanes, the PERMIT ONLY word pavement marking in white legend on a black background maybe used at some locations in conjunction with the LA28 word pavement marking, where engineering judgment determines it is needed. Guidance: 15 If used, the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings (see Figures 3B-107(LA28) and 3B-108(LA28)) should be in place before the games begin and maintained during the games for the time period June 1, 2028 to September 1, 2028. Standard: 16 Where used on roadways in GRN, the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings shall be removed after September 1, 2028 or the end of the games and the roadway restored to the condition of previous markings. Section 3A.02 Materials The following is added to this section: Support: 04 The chromaticity coordinates that define the ranges of acceptable colors, including the color white, for traffic control devices are found in the Appendix to Subpart F of 23 CFR 655. Standard: 05 The material used for the white color legend for the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings shall be retroreflective, as these pavement markings are traffic control devices under this Caltrans experimentation request specific application. Guidance: 06 The materials used for LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings should provide the white color through their temporary use period from June 1, 2028 to September 1, 2028. 07 Consideration should be given to selecting pavement marking materials that will minimize tripping or loss of traction for road users, including pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorcyclists.

pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 69 Chapter 3A - General July 15, 2026 Part 3 Markings Section 3A.03 Colors The following is added to this section: 02c Black color shall not be used as the legend color for the LA28 word message, when it is used on the pavement as a pavement marking, as the material used for black color is opaque and non-retroreflective. Option: 02d Black markings may be used in combination with the white color to enhance the contrast with a light-colored pavement. Standard: 04a When used, the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings shall be white color. Section 3A.05 Maintaining Minimum Pavement Marking Retroreflectivity The following is added to this section: Support: 09 The provisions of this Section requiring a method designed to maintain minimum pavement marking retroreflectivity do not apply to word pavement markings, which includes the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings (See CA MUTCD 2026 Section 3A.05, Paragraph 6).

pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 70 Chapter 3B - Pavement and Curb Markings July 15, 2026 Part 3 Markings CHAPTER 3B. PAVEMENT AND CURB MARKINGS Section 3B.21 Word Pavement Markings The following is added to this section: Support: 12 The LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings are used to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. These LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings can be helpful to road users in some locations by supplementing signs and providing additional emphasis, because the markings do not require diversion of the road user’s attention from the roadway surface. Option: 13 The LA28 word pavement markings may be used as determined by engineering judgment to supplement signs and/or to provide emphasis for regulatory and guide signs that have been modified by using the LA28 sign plaque or sign panel. The LA28 word pavement marking may be used alone, as a single line of information. 14 The PERMIT ONLY word pavement marking may be used in conjunction with the LA28 word pavement markings, as determined by engineering judgment to supplement signs and/or to provide additional emphasis for regulatory and guide signs that have been modified by using the LA28 sign plaque or sign panel. Standard: 15 The PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings shall not be used alone, it shall always be used in conjunction with the LA28 word pavement markings. 16 If used, the LA28 word pavement marking shall be in a single line. 17 If PERMIT ONLY word pavement marking is used in conjunction with the LA28 word pavement marking, it shall consist of three lines of information. Each word of the information, LA28, PERMIT and ONLY, shall constitute as a single separate line. These three lines of information shall read as LA28 PERMIT ONLY in the direction of travel, with the first word LA28, nearest to the road user (see Figure 3B-107(LA28)). 18 Detailed drawings of the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings and alphabet details are shown in Figure 3B- 108(LA28) and the “Standard Highway Signs and Markings” book. CA MUTCD 2026 Section 1A.05 contains information regarding how to obtain this publication. Standard: 19 If used, the LA28 word pavement marking shall be white legend. 20 If used, the PERMIT ONLY word pavement marking shall be white legend. 21 If used, the PERMIT ONLY word pavement marking shall not be used alone, it shall be used in conjunction with the LA28 word pavement marking. 22 The LA28 and PERMIT ONLY pavement marking letters and numerals shall be installed in accordance with the design details in the Pavement Markings chapter of the “Standard Highway Signs and Markings” book (see CA MUTCD 2026 Section 1A.05). Option: 23 The LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings may be proportionally scaled to fit within the width of the facility upon which they are applied. Guidance: 24 If used, each of the LA28, PERMIT and ONLY word pavement marking used on freeway and arterial streets segments in the GRN, should be spaced 50 feet apart, as shown in Figure 3B-107(LA28) Part B. 25 If used, each of the LA28, PERMIT and ONLY word pavement marking used on continuous lane segments in the GRN, should be spaced 250 feet apart, as shown in Figure 3B-108(LA28) Part C. 26 When used, the LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings letter heights should be as shown in Figure 3B-108(LA28).

pages.title: CHAPTER 3E. PREFERENTIAL LANE MARKINGS FOR MOTOR VEHICLES
pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 73 Chapter 3E - Preferential Lane Markings for Motor Vehicles July 15, 2026 Part 3 Markings CHAPTER 3E. PREFERENTIAL LANE MARKINGS FOR MOTOR VEHICLES Section 3E.02 Longitudinal Markings The following is added to this section: Support: 16 Using longitudinal markings that prohibit crossing between a GRN lane and the adjacent general-purpose lane triggers use of multiple overhead signs. Using a single solid white line, which discourages but does not prohibit crossing, between a GRN lane and the adjacent general-purpose lane (see Figure 3E-3) reduces the amount of required overhead signs. Refer to Chapter 2G for sign requirements. Section 3E.03 Preferential Lane Word and Symbol Markings The following is added to this section: Support: 15 Specific preferential lanes will be used to designate Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues on roadways that are included in the established GRN during LA28 in locations specified by the supplement. Specific preferential lanes that are used as dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues and included in the established GRN, are referred to as “GRN lane(s)” in this CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement. Standard: 16 The provisions of Chapter 3E for preferential lane word and symbol markings shall apply to all roadways included in the established GRN in locations specified by Caltrans experimentation request to FHWA. 17 When certain types of vehicles (such as without LA28 permit) are prohibited from using a GRN lane or when a GRN lane is restricted to use by only certain types of vehicles (such as with a LA28 permit) as an operational strategy, the LA28 word pavement marking alone, or in conjunction with the PERMIT ONLY word pavement marking shall be used to identify dedicated lanes on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. Option: 18 The LA28 and PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings may be omitted at toll plazas where physical conditions preclude the use of the markings. Guidance: 19 The location for the LA28, and if used, PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings should be based on engineering judgment that considers the prevailing speed, block lengths, distance from intersections, and other factors that affect clear communication to the road user. 20 If used, the spacing interval shown in Figure 3B-108(LA28) should be used based on the roadway classification. 21 The LA28, and if used, PERMIT ONLY word pavement markings should be placed on roadways in the established GRN at strategic locations such as major decision points, departures from the GRN lane, and along access to and from adjacent general- purpose lanes.

pages.title: CHAPTER 3G. DELINEATORS
pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 74 Chapter 3H - Colored Pavement July 15, 2026 Part 3 Markings CHAPTER 3G. DELINEATORS Section 3G.03 Application The following is added to this section: Support: 22 The provisions of Chapter 3G for delineators shall apply to all roadways included in the established GRN in locations specified by Caltrans experimentation request to FHWA. Option: 23 Delineators may be used on GRN roadways at locations where the alignment might be confusing or unexpected, to identify and separate dedicated lanes from general purpose lanes, to facilitate travel during LA28 games.

pages.title: PART 4
pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 75 Chapter 4B - Traffic Control Signals - General July 15, 2026 Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals PART 4 HIGHWAY TRAFFIC SIGNALS CHAPTER 4B. TRAFFIC CONTROL SIGNALS - GENERAL Section 4B.01 General The following is added to this section: Standard: 03 The provisions of Part 4 regarding highway traffic signals in general, features, faces, indications, phases, location and types, shall apply to all roadways included in the established GRN in locations specified by Caltrans experimentation request to FHWA. Support: 04 Any change to signal timing, signal phasing, signal coordination for coordinated mode in a progressive system for advanced signal synchronization, would be in accordance with Part 4 provisions. However, some aspects of these operational strategies deployed to coordinate and synchronize traffic signals for operational improvements, aren’t traffic control device policies and although related to the traffic control devices, they constitute engineering practices and are not covered by CA MUTCD.

pages.title: PART 6
pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 76 Chapter 6A - General July 15, 2026 Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control PART 6 TEMPORARY TRAFFIC CONTROL CHAPTER 6A. GENERAL Section 6A.03 TTC Devices The following is added to this section: Standard: 07 If used, the provisions for temporary traffic control devices in Part 6, shall apply to all temporary traffic control devices used on roadways included in the established GRN in locations specified by Caltrans experimentation request to FHWA.

pages.text: CA MUTCD 2026 LA28 Supplement Page 77 Chapter 6L - Other TTC Zone Traffic Control Devices July 15, 2026 Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control CHAPTER 6L. OTHER TTC ZONE TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES Section 6L.05 Portable Changeable Message Signs The following is added to this section: Standard: 39 If used, provisions of preferential and managed lane signs in Chapter 2G, changeable message signs in Chapter 2L and temporary traffic control in Part 6 of CA MUTCD 2026 and this LA28 Supplement shall apply to portable changeable message signs used in GRN dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues that is included in the established GRN. Support: 40 The information in this Section describes situations where the provisions for portable changeable message signs differ from those given in Chapter 2L. Option: 41 Portable changeable message signs may be used to display GRN messages, where engineering judgment determines the need to use GRN messages on GRN roadways to facilitate travel during LA28 games. Support: 42 Table 2L-102(LA28) provides examples of GRN messages for Portable CMS that can be used in GRN dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues that is included in the established GRN. Standard: 43 GRN messages used on portable changeable message signs shall be used only if the portable changeable message signs are located in or on approaches to GRN dedicated lane(s) for Olympic Games vehicles to travel between venues that is included in the established GRN. 44 Portable changeable message signs used on GRN roadways shall comply with the applicable design and application principles established in Chapter 2A.
